issues.current_text: Codex, que já tem 2 milhões de usuários ativos semanais e crescimento de 5x no uso desde janeiro
issues.previous_text: o Codex já tem 2 milhões de usuários semanais, 4x desde janeiro
issues.suggestion: Cut the Codex user stat entirely — it was reported two days ago. Only mention it if a materially new number exists (the 5x vs 4x discrepancy is suspicious and may be a hallucination). The Astral acquisition is genuinely new; let it stand on its own.

issues.current_text: Fidji Simo admitiu que espalhar recursos entre apps 'atrasou a execução'
issues.previous_text: A CEO de aplicações Fidji Simo disse em all-hands que a empresa 'não pode perder esse momento com side quests'
issues.suggestion: Fidji Simo's messaging was the lead story on 03-18. If the superapp merger is a new announcement, frame it as a new development without re-quoting Simo or re-explaining the internal pivot. One sentence of context ('after the strategic pivot reported Monday') is enough.

issues.current_text: A aquisição é resposta direta ao Claude Code, que vem atraindo desenvolvedores profissionais
issues.previous_text: A Anthropic virou o wake-up call que a OpenAI precisava... projetos como o browser Atlas e recursos de e-commerce entram em revisão enquanto Altman e Mark Chen repriorizam codificação e enterprise
issues.suggestion: The 'OpenAI reacts to Anthropic threat' narrative has been the frame on 03-18 and 03-19. The Astral acquisition IS new — lead with what Astral's tools do and why they matter for developer tooling, rather than framing it yet again as a defensive move against Claude Code.

issues.current_text: O Irã atacou a maior refinaria do Kuwait (730 mil barris/dia), o Qatar perdeu 17% da capacidade de GNL por até 5 anos, e drones atingiram a refinaria da Aramco em Yanbu
issues.previous_text: mísseis atingiram Ras Laffan no Catar — maior complexo de GNL do mundo, com produção paralisada e 20% do suprimento global cortado — e duas refinarias do Kuwait
issues.suggestion: Kuwait and Qatar attacks were the lead war story yesterday. The updated figures (17% capacity for 5 years, 730k bbl/day) are new data — keep those, but acknowledge this is an update, not a new event. Cut the description of what was already hit and focus on what changed: the Yanbu attack is new, the Tehran Nowruz bombing is new, the peace talks pause is new. Lead with those.

issues.current_text: Samsung anunciou investimento recorde de $73,3bi em capacidade e P&D para 2026, alta de 22% e acima dos ~$50bi de capex da TSMC. O objetivo é retomar a liderança em chips de IA da SK Hynix.
issues.previous_text: Samsung e AMD assinaram MOU para fornecimento de HBM4... o co-CEO Jun Young-hyun declarou que o setor vive um 'superciclo sem precedentes'... estreitaram a distância para a SK Hynix
issues.suggestion: Samsung has been a lead story for three consecutive days (Groq 3 fabrication on 03-18, HBM4 MOU on 03-19, $73B capex today). The $73B investment IS new, but the 'catch up with SK Hynix' framing was used yesterday. Either drop the SK Hynix comparison or find a different angle — e.g., compare with TSMC capex without repeating the rivalry narrative.

issues.current_text: dados da Ramp mostram que a Anthropic captura 73% de todo gasto de empresas comprando IA pela primeira vez
issues.previous_text: substituindo a Anthropic, rebaixada a risco na cadeia de suprimentos pelo DOD
issues.suggestion: The Ramp data is new, but placing it in the same paragraph as the OpenAI/Astral acquisition makes this the third consecutive edition where the OpenAI paragraph hinges on the Anthropic threat. Move the Ramp stat to a separate paragraph or a different section to avoid the impression that every OpenAI story is framed as 'Anthropic is winning, OpenAI reacts.'

issues.current_text: OpenAI compra Astral e funde tudo num superapp; [paragraph frames acquisition as 'resposta direta ao Claude Code' and cites Anthropic enterprise share]
issues.previous_text: A Anthropic virou o wake-up call que a OpenAI precisava. [paragraph frames Codex growth and pivot as response to Anthropic]
issues.suggestion: Three out of four editions frame OpenAI stories as 'reacting to Anthropic.' This has become a crutch. The Astral acquisition is interesting on its own (126M monthly downloads, ripgrep creator joining). Lead with the product story — what uv/Ruff/ty are, why they matter — rather than the competitive narrative readers have already absorbed.

issues.current_text: A guerra no Golfo segue escalando. O Irã atacou... Israel bombardeou... Trump diz que... o Pentágono discute...
issues.previous_text: Israel atacou instalações de South Pars... O Irã retaliou: mísseis atingiram Ras Laffan... Zelenskyy posicionou 201 especialistas... Trump aliviou sanções...
issues.suggestion: Four consecutive editions follow the same war paragraph template: list of targets hit → oil/energy impact → Western political response. Readers are numb to this pattern by now. Try a different entry point: lead with the strategic significance (e.g., 'three Gulf states' energy infrastructure has now been hit in 72 hours') or the economic fallout, rather than another target-by-target blow-by-blow.

issues.current_text: FDA aprovou o Wegovy HD (semaglutida 7,2mg)... perda de peso média de ~21% em 72 semanas... A Eli Lilly contra-atacou: o retatrutida... entregou 16,8% de perda de peso em 40 semanas
issues.previous_text: Structure Therapeutics reportou 16,3% de perda de peso com a pílula oral GLP-1 aleniglipron em 44 semanas — contra ~11% do orforglipron da Eli Lilly em 72
issues.suggestion: Both editions frame obesity drugs as a horse race (Company X delivered Y% weight loss vs Company Z's W%). The drugs are different but the structure is identical. Consider leading with the patient impact or the FDA's record 54-day approval instead of another percentage comparison table.

summary: High repetition: OpenAI-vs-Anthropic rivalry (3rd straight day), Codex stats recycled verbatim, Samsung-SK Hynix angle reused, Gulf war follows identical target-list template for 4th day, and weight loss drug coverage mirrors 03-17's percentage-comparison format.
